title: Patch: `cargo test` builds the AI optimised, as it already builds the engine and the cards
thread:
**Issue #2384 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #2384: Patch: `cargo test` builds the AI optimised, as it already builds the engine and the cards
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The automated tests that play games against the practice AI are among the slowest in the repository. They run the AI's search code with no compiler optimisation, while the game engine and cards it calls into are optimised. Turning optimisation on for the AI too should make those tests several times faster, with no change to any result. Every pull request then waits less for its checks, and the jobs that keep running over time get room.

## Why

- `Cargo.toml:58-83` sets a test opt-level of 2 for `jackioh-engine`, `jackioh-cards`, `jackioh-luau`, `mlua-sys`, `mlua`, `serde_json` and `indexmap`, but not for `jackioh-ai`. `git log -S"profile.test.package.jackioh-ai"` finds no attempt.
- AI-heavy tests are behind the recent over-time fixes:
  - `crates/server/tests/bots/seat.rs:853-857`: "one after another they took most of a minute, the last test `rust (test server)` waited on (#2323)", fixed by threads in #2343.
  - `crates/server/tests/api/practice.rs:233-238`: "each of its AI moves is a full search … held every test thread for over a minute, #2223".
- A job running over time is still an open issue (#2353).

## Proposal

- Add `[profile.test.package.jackioh-ai]` at opt-level 2, or 1 if that measures better once compile time is counted.
- Keep a comment with the measured numbers, as the engine's entry has.
- Debug assertions and overflow checks stay on in the test profile. Rust never reorders floating-point arithmetic at any opt-level, so the AI's decisions and every seeded result are unchanged.

## Where it lands

`Cargo.toml`, and a line in `crates/ai/README.md` if its test notes mention build speed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The PR reports before-and-after wall-clock times, build included, for:
  - `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`;
  - the server's AI-heavy tests (`--test server bots::`, `api::practice`);
  - `cargo test -p jackioh-tools`.
- [ ] Every test passes, with the same outcomes.
- [ ] No `rust (test …)` job on the PR is slower than the same job on `main`.

## Size and risks

A one-entry diff, but real measuring: medium.

- Jobs that build the AI but run little of it pay extra compile time. If those jobs regress, settle on opt-level 1, or drop the change and report the numbers.
- It may help #2353 but does not claim to close it.

---
Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it.

## Plan

_Written by `claude-4` (claude, `opus`, strong) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/40923656202)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

`cargo test` builds `jackioh-ai` at opt-level 1, by a new `[profile.test.package.jackioh-ai]` entry in the root `Cargo.toml` whose comment carries the measured numbers. Debug assertions and overflow checks stay on. The builder's final report gives before-and-after wall-clock times, build included, for `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`, the server's `bots::` and `api::practice::` tests and `cargo test -p jackioh-tools`, and shows every test passing with the same outcomes. Whether any `rust (test …)` job runs slower than on `main` can only be judged from the PR's CI.

**Level 1, not 2 (settled, the issue allows it).** The planner timed every `ci.yml` group that builds the AI on 4 cores, with the AI and every crate built on it compiled afresh each time. Totals in seconds, AI at 0 / 2 / 1:

| group | 0 | 2 | 1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| ai | 328 (14 build + 314 run) | 146 (80 + 66) | 130 (52 + 78) |
| ai slow | 107 | 107 | 100 |
| server | 151 | 145 | 140 |
| server api | 143 | 151 | 145 |
| server practice | 109 | 109 | 106 |
| server practice rulings | 113 | 111 | 110 |
| tools fuzz | 120 | 132 | 123 |
| tools duos, selfplay | 103 | 103 | 98 |
| tools, wasm | 86 | 90 | 85 |

Every group's `test result:` lines were identical at all three levels. Level 2 made three groups slower than 0 (`server api` +8, `tools fuzz` +12, `tools, wasm` +4). Level 1 was never more than 3 s slower than 0, which is within run-to-run noise. Level 2 is rejected.

## Files to touch

| Path | new/change | What |
|---|---|---|
| `Cargo.toml` | change | a new `[profile.test.package.jackioh-ai]` table, `opt-level = 1`, with its comment, between `[profile.test.package.indexmap]` and the `# The server and the WASM module…` comment |

Do not touch:
- `.github/` (no per-group `--config` in `ci.yml`).
- `crates/ai/README.md`: its Commands section says nothing about build speed, so the issue's optional README line does not apply.
- `Cargo.lock`, and any file under `crates/`, `apps/`, `spec/` or `scripts/`.
- `crates/cards/patches/`: this is an Internal change, so it needs no fragment, and `technical.json` is written on `main` by `patches log`.

No spec section or ruling governs this. CLAUDE.md rule 4 (purity) is untouched, since this is a build setting and no code changes. Rule 12 governs how the report names checks.

## Steps

1. **Write the timing script** at `/tmp/t2384/time.sh` (outside the repository), exactly:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# usage: bash /tmp/t2384/time.sh <before|after>   (run from the repository root)
set -u
export CARGO_TERM_COLOR=never CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0
out=/tmp/t2384/$1
mkdir -p "$out"
: > "$out/times.txt"
# item <name> <cargo args> [test filters]: the AI and every crate built on it compiled afresh
# (the engine, the cards and the Luau host do not depend on the AI), then the tests run.
item() {
  cargo clean -q -p jackioh-ai -p jackioh-server -p jackioh-tools -p jackioh-wasm -p jackioh-wasm-core -p jackioh-wasm-luau
  t0=$(date +%s)
  cargo test --no-run $2 > "$out/$1.build.log" 2>&1
  t1=$(date +%s)
  cargo test $2 -- ${3:-} > "$out/$1.run.log" 2>&1
  rc=$?
  t2=$(date +%s)
  echo "$1: build $((t1 - t0)) s, run $((t2 - t1)) s, total $((t2 - t0)) s, exit $rc" | tee -a "$out/times.txt"
  grep '^test result:' "$out/$1.run.log" | sed 's/; finished in.*//' > "$out/$1.results.txt"
}
item ai "-p jackioh-ai"
item server-ai "-p jackioh-server --test server" "bots:: api::practice::"
item tools "-p jackioh-tools"
```

   The filter `bots::` also matches `api::bots::`, as the issue's `--test server bots::` does.

2. **Warm the dependencies, untimed**, on the unchanged tree (so step 3 does not time building third-party crates):
   `cargo test --no-run -p jackioh-ai && cargo test --no-run -p jackioh-server --test server && cargo test --no-run -p jackioh-tools`

3. **Time "before"** on the unchanged tree: `bash /tmp/t2384/time.sh before`. It takes about 15 minutes. Every line of `/tmp/t2384/before/times.txt` must say `exit 0`. If one does not, stop and report it, because the failure is on `main`'s tree.

4. **Edit `Cargo.toml`.** After the line `opt-level = 2` that follows `[profile.test.package.indexmap]` (line 83), leave one blank line, then insert this exact block. Keep one blank line between it and the `# The server and the WASM module` comment:

```toml
# The practice AI at opt-level 1 (#2384), its debug assertions and overflow checks kept, as the
# engine's are: the AI's tests spend their time in its search, which ran unoptimised. On four cores,
# with the AI and every crate built on it compiled afresh, ci.yml's `ai` group took 328 s at 0
# (14 s compiling, 314 running), 130 s at 1 (52 and 78) and 146 s at 2 (80 and 66). No other group
# that builds the AI took over 3 s longer at 1 than at 0, while at 2 `server api` took 8 s and
# `tools fuzz` 12 s longer: compiling at 2 costs more than the little AI they run wins back.
[profile.test.package.jackioh-ai]
opt-level = 1
```

   Change nothing else in the file.

5. **Time "after"**: `bash /tmp/t2384/time.sh after`. It takes about 10 minutes.

6. **Compare outcomes**: `for i in ai server-ai tools; do diff /tmp/t2384/before/$i.results.txt /tmp/t2384/after/$i.results.txt && echo "$i same"; done`. It must print `ai same`, `server-ai same` and `tools same` with no diff lines. If any diff appears, revert step 4 and report the diff (see Risks).

7. **If an item's "after" total is larger than its "before" total**, re-run only that item both ways once to rule out noise:
   - Comment out the other two `item` lines in the script.
   - Run `after` (Cargo.toml as edited).
   - Temporarily undo step 4 and run `before`.
   - Redo step 4.

   Report both runs. If the item is still slower, keep level 1 anyway: the per-group table above is the decision's basis. Say so in the report.

8. **Run the checks** in the order the harness does. For this diff, `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims` must report kind `internal` and no problems. If it names a family that plays differently, stop: the AI's play changed with the opt-level, so revert step 4 and report it.

9. **Write the final report**, which becomes the PR description. It contains:
   - (a) A table of before/after build, run and total seconds for the three items, copied from both `times.txt` files, with the machine's `nproc`.
   - (b) The line "outcomes identical", with the `results.txt` lines of each item.
   - (c) The planner's per-group table from this plan, labelled as the planner's measurement, since the `Cargo.toml` comment quotes it.
   - (d) The decisions: level 1 over 2, with the numbers; no README line, since `crates/ai/README.md` has no build-speed note; no `ci.yml` change, since the bot may not edit `.github/`.
   - (e) That "no `rust (test …)` job slower than on `main`" is for a person to read off the PR's checks against `main`'s runs.

   For reference, the planner's run of this same script measured:

   | item | before (AI at 0): build + run = total | after (AI at 1): build + run = total |
   |---|---|---|
   | ai | 13 + 409 = 422 s | 52 + 155 = 207 s |
   | server-ai | 72 + 93 = 165 s | 76 + 60 = 136 s |
   | tools | 19 + 230 = 249 s | 31 + 196 = 227 s |

   All outcomes were identical. Do not report these numbers as your own.

## Tests

No new test. A build-profile setting has no behaviour a unit test could assert: such a test could only re-read `Cargo.toml`, which proves nothing about speed or results. The proof is:
- the before/after outcome diff of step 6, which must be empty, over these commands:
  - `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`
  - `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server -- bots:: api::practice::`
  - `cargo test -p jackioh-tools`
- the harness's `cargo test --workspace --features jackioh-engine/testkit,jackioh-engine/ts`, which must pass with no change under `apps/web/src/wire`.

## Done when

- [ ] `Cargo.toml` holds the step 4 block exactly, and `git diff --stat` shows `Cargo.toml` as the only changed file.
- [ ] Both `times.txt` files have three lines, each `exit 0`, and step 6 prints three `same` lines.
- [ ] The harness's checks are green: rustfmt, catalog, patches, rulings, clippy, cargo tests (wire unchanged), web tests. `classify --claims` shows kind `internal` with no problems.
- [ ] The final report holds items (a) to (e) of step 9 and names any red check by its name (CLAUDE.md rule 12).

## Risks

- **Determinism and replay.** The opt-level changes no result:
  - Rust never enables fast-math, contraction or reassociation at any opt-level.
  - The AI's float work is `+`, `*`, `/`, `sqrt` (exact), `exp` on run-time values (`decide.rs:298`) and `powf(DEAL_SHAPE_K)` (`shadow_ban.rs:1504`), and LLVM rewrites none of these without fast-math.
  - The AI is pure, with budgets in nodes and not time, so faster code plays the same moves.
  - Every group's outcomes matched at 0, 1 and 2.
  - Only the test profile changes, so the release server and the WASM module (opt-level 3) do not change.

  If step 6 or `classify` ever disagrees, the change is wrong: revert it and report.
- **Compile cost in groups that run little AI.** These are `server api`, `tools fuzz` and `tools, wasm`. They measured within 3 s at level 1. In CI the AI compiles next to the cards, which also wait only on the engine, so its cost there is at most what was measured. If CI shows such a job slower than on `main`, the remedy is a person's: add `--config profile.test.package.jackioh-ai.opt-level=0` to that group's `test:` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, as `tools fuzz` already does for `jackioh-luau`.
- **The `db` job's store-contract build** (`crates/server/tests/db/run.sh`, `--profile test`) compiles the AI at 1, about 10 s more. That job runs on `main` pushes only, and it is not a `rust (test …)` job.
- **Daily coverage** (`super.yml`, llvm-cov over engine, cards and ai). Coverage counters are inserted before optimisation, and the engine and the cards already run at 2 there, so the floor is not at risk.
- **Timing noise.** Runs varied by up to about 8 s at the same level. Step 7 handles an item that comes out slower.

## Open questions

None blocks the build. A person judges the third acceptance item ("no `rust (test …)` job slower than on `main`") from the PR's checks, and adds the per-group `ci.yml` override above only if one regresses. The bot may not change `.github/`.
````
